issue1LanguageClaimAuthorityTrace.allowedSourceMaterialDefinition: Contains overview, keywords, and sourceRefs; spoken-language authority is conveyed via facts.spokenLanguages under production governance (editorial-writer.v1.1.md and source-boundary-risk-verifier.v1.1.md).
issue1LanguageClaimAuthorityTrace.finding: Rule A correctly scanned the copy and treated Russian as authorized because facts.spokenLanguages contains "Russian", which was visible in the review packet (- **Languages**: Russian). The human reviewer note was an empirical reviewer perception error, which has now been corrected under approved human correction artifact (removing the Russian-language defect finding and preserving whyWatch byte-for-byte). Under production governance, facts.spokenLanguages is authoritative; Rule A correctly produces no false hits.
issue1LanguageClaimAuthorityTrace.title: Guardians

issue2TheFourthKindEvaluation.genericNormalization: Rule B incorporates generic calendar-decade grounding (\b\d{4}s\b / \b(?:1[89]|20)\d0s\b) to recognize source-supported decade spans without title-specific rules.
issue2TheFourthKindEvaluation.humanReviewReason: Director "Olatunde Osunsanmi" and location "Nome, Alaska" match exactly, and the Description faithfully restates the authorized overview. However, the Why-watch claim that the film "reframes real-world missing-persons cases" asserts that the film is grounded in actual real-world events — this echoes the film's well-known (and disputed) marketing claim of being "based on true events," which is not part of the authorized overview provided here. The overview presents the disappearances and Dr. Tyler's investigation as the film's internal premise, not as a claim about real-world cases; asserting this is an external/pre-training detail rather than an authorized fact. Additionally, the Curiosity hook specifies "nighttime traumas" — a specific detail about the timing/nature of patients' experiences that is not stated in the authorized overview (which says only that Tyler "finds evidence of alien abductions" while treating patients). Recommend removing the "real-world" framing from Why-watch and softening the hook to remove the invented "nighttime" specificity.
issue2TheFourthKindEvaluation.overviewText: Since the 1960s, a disproportionate number of the population in and around Nome, Alaska, have gone missing. Despite FBI investigations, the disappearances remain a mystery. Dr. Abigail Tyler, a psychologist, may be on the verge of blowing the unsolved cases wide open when, during the course of treating her patients, she finds evidence of alien abductions.
issue2TheFourthKindEvaluation.semanticTemporalGrounding: The phrase "Since the 1960s" in the authorized overview semantically grounds multi-decade duration ("decades"). The human reviewer explicitly accepted the Description as faithful and did not cite "decades" as a defect.
issue2TheFourthKindEvaluation.title: The Fourth Kind

methodologicalCaveats: All metrics represent APPARENT_RETROSPECTIVE_PERFORMANCE on the 30-record development set.
These records were already inspected to identify defect categories; this evaluation does not constitute independent validation.
Candidate-routing apparent performance (would the rule route this candidate to human review?) is separated from rule-hit defect concordance (does the rule hit reflect a confirmed defect?).
Unbiased performance confirmation requires future independent prospective blinded holdout records.
Production routing was NOT modified by this experiment.

coreGapsCovered: Interrogative sentences in curiosityHook that presuppose unstated story facts must be evaluated as assertive claims.
allowedSourceMaterial is the exclusive ground truth; raw metadata arrays (e.g. facts.keywords) not in allowedSourceMaterial do not authorize copy.
Remove or strictly qualify prompt exceptions around metaphorical urgency and genre register.
Add explicit schema categories for UNAUTHORIZED_LANGUAGE_OR_NATIONALITY and SPECULATIVE_HOOK_PREMISE.
